dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: A full eight-leg effort costs ~28 paste blocks across 8 stops — 4 of those stops are pure relay on legs needing no human judgment — because `commands/next.md:51-61` requires `next` to show its waybill verbatim and stop, so waybill cannot advance an effort while the operator is away from the keyboard.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Under `--autopilot`, halts drop from 8 to 3 on the legs `next` can reach, a complete route walk costs at most 6 invocations, and the longest unattended run rises from 0 legs to 2 (`specs` + `execute`) — each figure pinned by a named test in the fixture walk.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Every mechanical check puts its whole assertion in the runnable half — golden stability is `git diff --exit-code`, and per-criterion teeth come from `--test-name-pattern` piped to `grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'`, since `node --test` exits 0 printing `# pass 0` when a pattern matches nothing.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: MVP is the route's gate field, `next` executing, `status`'s in-bay answer carrying the waybill, `--autopilot`, the failed-stamp ask and the mismatch warning; the booking-level override and subagent dispatch sit in Full; six exclusions are named explicitly, four of them by the operator.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The one contradiction found — `ideate` being a gate whose stamp cannot flip when conducted — proved unreachable: `src/cli.js:278` never issues an `ideate` waybill and `src/legs.js:131` marks it done whenever a docket is open, so its gate flag is documentation-only and the three gates `next` can reach all have stamps that flip when conducted.

problem: Waybill's `next` reports; it does not drive. `commands/next.md:51-61` instructs the session to show the CLI's waybill block verbatim and stop — "It is already the whole answer" — and running the commands it lists is explicitly the next session's job. The only override is a `RUN:` line, which the CLI prints only when the operator has already pasted `/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>` after clearing. Every leg boundary on the eight-leg route is therefore a manual relay.

That relay costs roughly 28 paste blocks per effort: each `handover: transfer` leg renders `/clear`, `/model`, `/effort` and the command; each `through` leg renders three. Eight legs, eight stops. Four of those stops — `bay`, `specs`, `execute`, `cleanup` — ask nothing of the operator's judgment; they are pure transport, and the operator is the conveyor belt.

The sharpest cost is not keystrokes but presence. Because nothing advances without a paste, an effort cannot progress while the operator is away, even across `specs` and `execute` — the two longest legs on the route, and the two that most obviously want to run unattended. A route designed to be walked in sessions currently requires a human at every session boundary, including the boundaries that exist only for context hygiene.
goals: Under `--autopilot`, halt exactly once per gate the command can reach — three halts (`refine`, `contract`, `review`) rather than today's eight — and never halt for transport.

Walk a complete eight-leg route in at most 6 `/waybill:next` invocations, down from ~28 paste blocks; the fourth operator stop belongs to `/waybill:new` conducting `ideate` and is unchanged by this work.
Raise the longest unattended run from 0 legs to 2, so `specs` and `execute` cross without the operator present.
Make gate membership explicit data — a `gate` field on the route — rather than prose scattered across `commands/*.md`.
Preserve the context hygiene that `handover: transfer` buys: a leg whose booking names a more capable model than the running session must never run degraded in silence.

mvp.item: A `gate` field on the route in `src/legs.js`, true for `ideate`, `refine`, `contract` and `review`
mvp.reason: Everything else keys off it; gate membership must be data, not prose. `ideate`'s flag is documentation-only — `next` never reaches that leg.

mvp.item: `/waybill:next` executes the next leg — invoking its carrier in-session rather than printing paste blocks
mvp.reason: The core verb change; the whole point

mvp.item: `/waybill:next` conducts a gate leg and then stops, crossing nothing after it
mvp.reason: "Take me to the next human gate, then walk me through it" — the gate is conducted, not merely arrived at

mvp.item: `/waybill:status`'s in-bay answer gains the waybill paste blocks; the trunk fleet listing keeps none
mvp.reason: The manual relay must stay reachable or a model mismatch has no escape hatch. The fleet listing never carried a waybill and must not start.

mvp.item: `/waybill:next --autopilot` crosses non-gate legs until a gate, conducts it, and stops
mvp.reason: Where the unattended reach comes from — it crosses `specs` and `execute`

mvp.item: Stop-and-ask when a crossed leg runs but its stamp does not flip: one prompt offering retry, inspect, or stop
mvp.reason: The only thing preventing a runaway loop; chosen over a silent halt so a failure becomes a decision

mvp.item: A non-gate leg booked `handover: transfer` is dispatched to a subagent at its booked model; `through` legs run in-session; gate legs are never dispatched
mvp.reason: `transfer` already means "this leg wants its own fresh context", and a subagent is exactly that. This is how autopilot crosses `specs` and `execute` at all — without it MVP autopilot crosses nothing worth crossing.

mvp.item: A run log naming, per crossed leg, the model it actually ran at
mvp.reason: The only way a dispatched leg and an in-session one are told apart after an unattended run

mvp.item: `cleanup` pre-flight: crossable when the bay is clean, halting with the ask on a dirty worktree, unpushed commits or an unmerged branch; gitignored papers deleted but named in the log
mvp.reason: Pre-approving cleanup's destructive git steps is what lets one autopilot run finish an effort; the pre-flight is what keeps that from discarding real work unattended

mvp.item: Sweep every prose surface describing `next` as show-and-stop — repo-root README, docs/guide, commands/*.md, src/help.js — and add the missing root-README assertion to the suite
mvp.reason: docs/ideation/learnings.md records this exact gap from next-from-anywhere, and no test today reads the repo-root README at all

mvp.item: Update `docs/guide/03-reference.md` in the same phase as each new booking key and CLI flag
mvp.reason: tests/guide.test.js:202-206 asserts every booking key and every USAGE flag appears there, so deferring the doc reddens the suite in the phase that adds the key

full.item: A `gate:` key in booking frontmatter overriding the route default in either direction
full.reason: Lets a solo operator un-gate `review` on their own machine; per-machine preference, not load-bearing for the paste-count goals

stretch.item: `--autopilot --dry-run`: print the run autopilot would make, and where it would stop, without running anything

outOfScope.reason: A subagent takes `model` but not `effort`; a dispatched `execute` runs opus-at-default rather than opus/high. Accepted and documented rather than worked around.

outOfScope.item: Splicing non-stock legs into the route via `after:`
outOfScope.reason: Already deliberately deferred to Future in commit 0c5c5fc; overlays rebook and re-gate the eight stock legs, never add a ninth

outOfScope.item: Fleet-wide autopilot across several open dockets
outOfScope.reason: One docket per invocation, as `next` works today

outOfScope.item: Any retry beyond the single ask — no backoff, no automatic second attempt, no repair logic
outOfScope.reason: One attempt per leg keeps the failure mode legible

outOfScope.item: Changing `ideate`'s stamp or giving it a paper
outOfScope.reason: `next` never reaches `ideate` (src/cli.js:278, src/legs.js:131), and a paper written before `bay` exists would land in the main checkout — the one thing waybill's design prevents
`new` already conducts `ideate` and stops; the scope named was next, status and autopilot

outOfScope.item: Discovering the running session's model, and any model-capability ranking table
outOfScope.reason: Nothing in src/ can learn the session's model — only HOME, WAYBILL_BAY_DIR and WAYBILL_BOOKINGS_DIR are read anywhere — and a haiku<sonnet<opus table would go stale each model generation. `handover: transfer` is the trigger instead.

future: Detecting session cleanliness rather than assuming it, if assuming-clean proves wrong in practice
Making `effort` settable on a dispatched subagent, should the harness ever expose it
A gate that is situational rather than static — a leg becoming a gate because a stamp returned STAMP_UNKNOWN or a diff crossed a size threshold

phases.title: The gate field
phases.notes: Add `gate` to the LEGS entries in src/legs.js and expose it through resolveLeg. Pure data; no behaviour change. Also documents the gate column in docs/guide/03-reference.md's route table and in src/help.js's ROUTE, so the concept is never introduced silently. The booking-level `gate:` key is phase 5, and that is where tests/guide.test.js:206's booking-key coupling bites.

phases.title: status carries the waybill
phases.notes: Larger than a renderer move: status() rejects every argument today by design (src/cli.js:316-321), so it gains --markdown, its bang line in commands/status.md:33 changes (pinned by tests/commands.test.js), tests/golden/status.txt moves, and docs/guide/03-reference.md gains the flag. Renders the in-bay waybill via renderWaybillMarkdown with no content change to any existing golden; the trunk fleet listing keeps no waybill. Rewrites commands/status.md:45-49, which today forbids exactly this. Lands before next stops printing so the relay is never unreachable.

phases.title: next executes the leg
phases.notes: The verb change. The CLI emits a run literal for a non-gate leg and a gate literal for a gate; commands/next.md acts on those literals, never on the session's reading, preserving the rule at next.md:68-69. Drops the `named`-only gating on ENTER BAY:/RUN: (src/cli.js:161-165, src/waybill.js:364-368) so a bare `/waybill:next` also emits them. A `through` leg runs in-session; a non-gate `transfer` leg is dispatched to a subagent at its booked model; a gate leg is always conducted in-session.

phases.title: autopilot, the failed-stamp ask, and cleanup pre-flight
phases.notes: --autopilot crosses non-gate legs, re-deriving state after each, conducts the gate it reaches, stops. One ask when a crossed leg fails to stamp, never a retry. Pre-approves cleanup's destructive git steps behind a pre-flight that halts on a dirty worktree, unpushed commits or an unmerged branch. Autopilot assumes the session is clean enough to cross two legs — crossing a `transfer` leg in a subagent is what makes that safe. Settles whether --autopilot combines with a named target, given commands/next.md:47 passes "$ARGUMENTS" as one quoted token and src/cli.js:225-231 reads any non-dash positional as a branch. Adds docs/guide/03-reference.md for the flag, and tests/autopilot.test.js with the named cases the criteria grep for. Crossing depends on the user-level /spec:* command links and `openspec` on PATH; a carrier that will not resolve surfaces as the single ask, not a stall.

phases.title: The booking-level gate override
prereqs: autopilot, the failed-stamp ask, and cleanup pre-flight
phases.notes: Full tier. Accept `gate:` in booking frontmatter (src/bookings.js OPTIONAL) and resolve booking-over-route in src/inference.js, with tests pinning both override directions. Adds the key to docs/guide/03-reference.md in this phase for the same guide-test reason as phase 1.

phases.title: The prose sweep
prereqs: autopilot, the failed-stamp ask, and cleanup pre-flight
phases.notes: Grep every surface describing next as show-and-stop — repo-root README, docs/guide/*, commands/*.md, src/help.js — and update it. Extend tests/guide.test.js to read the repo-root README, which no test reads today, asserting the new verb is present as well as the old phrasing gone.
